text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak told an economic conference of the ruling National Democratic Party that Jerusalem was the most serious part of the Israeli-Palestinian issue and any misjudged mistake in dealing with it early would arouse anger. He said that Israel's patronising language was unacceptable and that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's proposal to jump to "final status" talks would lead to a vicious circle.
- Mubarak told Israeli television that Egypt did not prefer any one Israeli government over any other but it wanted an Israeli government capable of fulfilling its commitments.
- Mubarak received a report from Foreign Minister Amr Moussa on developments in the region.
- Mubarak received a message from Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma and Ukrainian Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko said Mubarak had accepted an invitation to visit Ukraine.
- The council of the Arab League will today discuss the question of Jerusalem.
- Mubarak will today receive Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and four Arab foreign ministers.
- Mubarak said it was impossible to control people who have been wronged and oppressed. He told Israeli television that Israel was responsible for instability in the region.
- Tomorrow is the deadline for submitting tax returns. For the first time in 30 years there will be fine for failing to submit one.
- Mubarak said that violence will end only when Israel stops building settlements, that Jersualem is of concern to all religions and that building the Abu Ghneim settlement was "playing with fire".

- A draft resolution for the Arab League foreign ministers' meeting calls for freezing normalisation with Israel and maintaining the economic boycott until there is a comprehensive and just peace on all tracks.
